channel.title: Engineering Digest
channel.description: Daily digest of engineering blog posts from top tech companies

item.title: Agents aren’t humans (but they kinda are)
item.description: AI agents act for millions, but servers see intermediaries that strip user visibility This post defines the problem space and introduces a collaborative approach to safely identifying, allowing, and managing this automated traffic.

item.title: Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub
item.description: GitHub now highlights ACCESSIBILITY.md files and helps maintainers document accessibility goals, known barriers, supported environments, contributor expectations, and reporting processes The post Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

item.title: Reflex: an architecture for building mobile apps with agents
item.description: Our architecture lets agents test mobile app behavior without an emulator and use one test suite to keep iOS and Android in sync.

item.title: How two engineer side projects became the agent taking action inside Dropbox
item.description: Two side projects explored a new way to get work done with files already in Dropbox Here’s how engineers brought them together and turned those experiments into a new customer experience.

item.title: How AI-assisted development helped us build the new Dropbox experience
item.description: From sharing features across web and desktop to testing the details customers depend on, this is how AI-assisted development helped our engineers deliver the updated Dropbox experience.

item.title: Analyze your Stripe data directly with your agent
item.description: You can now use natural language to create an investor slide deck highlighting where your business outperformed in the previous quarter, or build a custom dashboard to understand why your Stripe revenue changed.

item.title: Amazon S3 Tables now offer managed migration of Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg
item.description: You can now migrate existing Apache Hive datasets in Amazon S3 to fully managed Apache Iceberg tables in Amazon S3 Tables, with no pipelines to build or compute to provision, while production workloads keep running.
